title: Taskboard (whole system)
description: Internal team task tracker: a FastAPI API (only component touching PostgreSQL, Redis and attachment storage) behind a Node.js Express UI server that renders pages and authenticates browser users. Features: email/password accounts with reset links, admin user management, teams, projects with outbound status-change webhooks, tasks with Markdown, comments, attachments up to 10 MB, search with client-chosen sort, CSV export, activity feeds.
author: Claude Code session (arm A), from sec-review perform_threat_model context; statuses updated at wrap-up
data_touched: User credentials: email, Argon2id password hash (users table)
Opaque session tokens: SHA-256 hash in sessions table, raw value only in the browser's HttpOnly cookie and in UI-to-API Authorization headers
Password reset tokens: SHA-256 hash in password_reset_tokens, raw value in outbox rows and API log (dev mailer)
Personal data: display names and emails of users, visible to teammates and admins
Task content, Markdown descriptions and comments, labels, due dates
Attachment bytes (local volume or S3) and original filenames
Project webhook URLs and outbound webhook payloads
Service secrets: UI-to-API service token, cookie/CSRF secret, DB password, Redis auth token

threats.what_can_go_wrong: A member of team A changes the task, project, comment or attachment id in a URL and reads or edits team B's data, because a handler loads the object by id without checking team membership.
threats.mitigation: A single AccessPolicy service resolves every object to its team and checks membership (or admin) before any read or write; non-members get 404. Search and list queries join on team_members for the caller. Integration tests cover cross-team access for every resource type.

references.description: All task/comment/attachment endpoints take bare UUIDs; team membership is the only boundary
AccessPolicy resolves every object to its team; non-members get NotFoundError; tests/integration/test_work_api.py::test_cross_team_access_is_not_found probes 13 endpoints

threats.what_can_go_wrong: A member calls PATCH /api/v1/admin/users/{id} or creates/archives a project directly against the API (or via a crafted form post to the UI) because only the UI hides the buttons.
threats.impact: Privilege escalation to admin; unauthorised project changes.
threats.mitigation: Role and ownership checks live in services (AdminService requires admin; ProjectService requires team owner or admin). Request schemas use extra='forbid' so role cannot be set at registration or profile update.

references.description: Admin-only and owner-only operations exist alongside member operations
require_admin/team_for_manager in services; RequestModel extra='forbid' (api/schemas/common.py); role taken from DB each request (F-080)

threats.what_can_go_wrong: An attacker sets a project's webhook URL to http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ or an internal service (api:8000, redis, RDS) and the API's background sender POSTs to it, or a public hostname that later resolves (DNS rebinding) or redirects to an internal address.
threats.impact: SSRF into the VPC; on EC2 with IMDSv1 this could leak instance role credentials.
threats.mitigation: Validate scheme (https only unless explicitly allowed in dev), resolve the host at send time, reject loopback/private/link-local/multicast/reserved/CGNAT/metadata addresses, connect to the validated IP with the original Host header and SNI, never follow redirects, short connect/read timeouts, cap response read. Enforce IMDSv2 with hop limit 1 on EC2.

references.description: API sends webhook POSTs from a background thread to user-configured URLs
https only, all resolved addresses must be global, connection pinned to the checked IP, no redirects, 64 KiB cap, attempt deadline (F-073); EC2 IMDSv2 hop limit 1 (infra/modules/*/main.tf)

threats.what_can_go_wrong: A teammate writes a task description or comment containing
threats.impact: Account actions performed as other users, including admins.
data_affected: all data the victim can reach
threats.mitigation: Render Markdown with marked, then sanitize-html with a strict tag/attribute allow-list and http/https/mailto-only links; EJS auto-escaping everywhere else (no <%- except sanitized HTML); strict CSP without inline script.

references.description: UI renders Markdown to sanitized HTML
marked + sanitize-html allow-list, http/https/mailto only, forced rel; CSP script-src 'none' (ui/src/app.ts); 9 XSS vectors unit-tested

threats.what_can_go_wrong: A user uploads an .html or .svg attachment; another user opens it and it renders inline in the UI origin, running script.
threats.mitigation: Downloads are always Content-Disposition: attachment with Content-Type application/octet-stream and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, plus a sandbox CSP on the download response. Any file type is allowed by the brief, so no type allow-list.

references.description: Attachments are any type and downloadable with their original filename
download_attachment: application/octet-stream, Content-Disposition attachment, nosniff, CSP sandbox; UI sendDownload repeats them

threats.what_can_go_wrong: An uploaded filename like ../../etc/passwd or a name with CR/LF or quotes is used in a storage path or echoed into the Content-Disposition header.
threats.impact: File overwrite on the API host; response header injection.
threats.mitigation: Storage keys are server-generated UUIDs; the local storage resolves paths and checks they stay under the root. Original filename is stored only as metadata, reduced to its basename, stripped of control characters, and emitted with RFC 6266/5987 filename* encoding.

references.description: stores attachment bytes on a local volume or S3 under random keys
clean_filename, server-generated keys checked by infra/storage/base.py check_key, RFC 6266 content_disposition

threats.what_can_go_wrong: A client uploads many multi-gigabyte bodies or a slow stream to exhaust disk or memory on the UI or API.
threats.mitigation: UI multer limit of 10 MB and one file; API rejects Content-Length over limit and counts bytes while streaming, aborting past 10 MB.

references.description: up to 10 MB each
BodySizeLimitMiddleware (256 KB JSON, 10 MB upload, F-074) and byte counter in AttachmentService; multer limits in ui/src/controllers/TaskController.ts

threats.what_can_go_wrong: Attackers run credential stuffing against /auth/login, or hammer /auth/password/forgot to spam the outbox.
threats.mitigation: Per-email and per-client-IP fixed-window rate limits on login and forgot-password (Redis-backed, in-memory fallback), Argon2id hashing, minimum 12-character passwords with a 128 limit, generic error text.

references.description: UI forwards X-Client-IP so the API can rate-limit per client
per (email, IP) lockout + per-account ceiling (F-070), per-IP limits, password-change throttle (F-075), Argon2id

threats.what_can_go_wrong: Reset tokens are guessable, reusable, long-lived, or the reset link points at an attacker host because it was built from the Host header; or forgot-password reveals which emails exist.
threats.mitigation: secrets.token_urlsafe(32) tokens stored as SHA-256, 30-minute expiry, single use, all sessions revoked on reset, link built from configured PUBLIC_BASE_URL, forgot always returns 202 with the same body.

references.description: Forgot password: request a reset link by email, then set a new password using the link
forgot_password/reset_password: 256-bit token, SHA-256 at rest, 30 min, atomic consume, PUBLIC_BASE_URL links, same 202 response

threats.what_can_go_wrong: Any process on the internal network (or a compromised container) calls the API directly with forged identity headers, or a stolen session token keeps working after logout, password change or deactivation.
threats.mitigation: Identity is never taken from a header: the API resolves the Bearer session token against the sessions table on every request and checks the user is active. The UI must also present X-Service-Token, compared in constant time. Logout deletes the session; password change/reset and deactivation delete all of the user's sessions.

references.description: Authorization: Bearer <session token>, X-Service-Token
require_service_auth (constant-time), identity only from the DB session lookup; sessions deleted on logout/password change/reset/deactivation

threats.what_can_go_wrong: Another website auto-submits a form to the UI (e.g. remove member, change password) using the victim's cookie.
threats.mitigation: SameSite=Lax HttpOnly cookies (Secure and __Host- prefix in production) plus a per-session HMAC CSRF token on every POST form, verified by middleware.

references.description: session token in an HttpOnly SameSite cookie
HMAC-bound token on every POST with a per-purpose key (F-087), Sec-Fetch-Site check, SameSite=Lax and __Host- cookies

threats.what_can_go_wrong: The client-supplied sort field is interpolated into SQL (ORDER BY {field}), or free-text search builds LIKE patterns by string concatenation.
threats.mitigation: Sort field is validated against an enum mapped to ORM column objects; direction is an enum; search uses bound parameters with LIKE wildcards escaped.

references.description: sort by any task field in either direction, with field and direction supplied by the client
_SORT_COLUMNS enum map, escape_like with bound parameters; injection attempt returns 422 in tests

threats.what_can_go_wrong: A task title starting with =HYPERLINK(...) or =cmd|... is exported to CSV and executes when a teammate opens it in a spreadsheet.
threats.impact: Code execution or data exfiltration on the victim's workstation.
threats.mitigation: Prefix cells beginning with = + - @ tab or CR with a single quote.

references.description: Export a project's tasks as CSV
neutralise_cell prefixes = + - @ tab CR with a quote

threats.what_can_go_wrong: A cached team or project list or task detail is served to a user who was removed from the team, or cached data keyed only by object id bypasses the membership check.
threats.mitigation: Authorization runs against the database before any cache read; per-user list caches are invalidated on member add/remove; cache values are JSON, never pickle.

references.description: uses Redis for cache-aside reads
membership checked in PostgreSQL before/after cache reads; role and active flag always from the DB (F-080); JSON values only

threats.what_can_go_wrong: Reset links and session tokens are written to logs, which are shipped to a log store readable by more people than the database.
threats.mitigation: Session tokens and passwords are never logged. The brief requires emails to be written to the API log, so the dev mailer logs the reset email; this is accepted for this build and documented, with a real mailer replacing it in production.
threats.accepted_risk: Required by the brief: there is no real email provider and emails must be readable from the API log in dev and tests.

references.description: write outgoing emails to the API log and to an outbox table
LogOutboxMailer logs reset emails as the brief requires

threats.what_can_go_wrong: The first-admin management command ships a default password, or secrets are baked into images or committed in .env files.
threats.mitigation: Command reads email and password from env vars, refuses empty or short passwords, no defaults. Secrets only in env/SSM; .env git-ignored and .dockerignore'd; no build args for secrets.

references.description: Secrets ... come from environment variables populated from AWS SSM Parameter Store at boot
create-admin reads env only, 12+ characters; no default accounts; secrets generated into .env / SSM

threats.what_can_go_wrong: Traffic between ALB and UI, UI and API, or API and RDS/ElastiCache is sniffed inside the VPC.
threats.impact: Session token and credential disclosure to a network-positioned attacker.
threats.mitigation: TLS 1.2+ policy on the ALB with HTTP->HTTPS redirect; RDS with forced SSL (rds.force_ssl) and sslmode=verify-full against the RDS CA bundle; ElastiCache transit encryption required with an AUTH token. UI-to-API stays HTTP inside private subnets restricted by security groups; accepted for this build and documented.
threats.accepted_risk: UI-to-API hop is plain HTTP inside private subnets locked to the UI security group; adding internal TLS needs a private CA, out of scope for this build.

references.description: ALB --HTTP--> UI server ... calls the API over the private network
ALB TLS 1.2+ with redirect; RDS verify-full; ElastiCache TLS required; UI->API HTTP inside private subnets

threats.what_can_go_wrong: A webhook receiver for project A, holding the signing secret, forges status-change events to project B's receiver; or, without any shared secret, receivers cannot verify events at all.
threats.impact: Spoofed task events trigger downstream automation.
threats.mitigation: Each project gets its own key HMAC(WEBHOOK_SIGNING_SECRET, 'project:'+id), shown only to the team owner and admins; X-Taskboard-Signature signs every body (F-077).

references.description: project_signing_key and sign(); integration test verifies the signature with the key from the project response

threats.what_can_go_wrong: A compromised UI instance reads the API's SSM SecureStrings (database URL, Redis token) or the migration password, because a broad managed policy grants ssm:GetParameter on every parameter.
threats.impact: Database and cache access from the internet-facing tier.
threats.mitigation: No AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore; a minimal Session Manager policy; kms:Decrypt bound to each service's own parameter ARNs via the KMS encryption context (F-090).

references.description: session_manager policy and DecryptOwnConfig condition on kms:EncryptionContext:PARAMETER_ARN

summary: 19 threats. 17 mitigated in code and infrastructure, 2 accepted (TM-15 reset links in the dev mail log, required by the brief; TM-17 plain HTTP between UI and API inside private subnets). TM-18 and TM-19 were added during the build from post-coding reviews. Archive extraction threats from the library do not apply: the app never extracts uploads.
